source: Condensed from the Unimig Razor 205 Smart Set manual troubleshooting charts (pp.40–43), reworded

fixes: Wire speed or voltage too high – turn down
Wrong polarity for the wire (gasless = DCEN)
Stick-out too long – keep 5–10 mm
Dirty metal or rusty/oily wire – clean back to bright metal
Gas flow wrong or draughty – check hose/leaks, shield from wind
Wrong gas, gas off, or leaks – check cylinder, hose, Euro O-ring
Flow too low or too high, or wind blowing gas away
Moisture, paint, oil or mill scale on the job
Nozzle clogged with spatter, or diffuser missing/damaged
Contaminated wire
Voltage too low – increase
Wire speed too high – decrease
Torch held too far away – keep 5–10 mm stick-out

mig.problem: Weld sitting on top / lack of fusion
fixes: Not enough heat – more voltage and matching wire speed
Keep the arc on the leading edge of the pool, 5–15° gun angle
Aim at the joint; pause on the side walls when weaving
Clean the base metal
Too much heat – drop voltage/wire speed
Travel faster
Not enough heat – more voltage/wire speed, slow down
Joint too thick or poorly prepped – bevel/gap so the arc reaches the root
Keep the arc on the leading edge, 5–10 mm stick-out
Selector on MIG?
Standard / Spool gun switch on the right setting?
Liner worn or clogged – most common cause; blow out, ideally replace
Contact tip worn or wrong size
Drive roller wrong size/type (flux-core needs knurled), worn, or wire not in the groove
Roller pressure too high (flattens wire) or spool brake too tight
Torch lead kinked or bent too sharply; soft/small wire hates long leads
Wire tangled on the spool, or dirty wire
Wrong polarity, or wire speed / voltage way off
Torch on DC+ – must be DC− (torch negative)
No/wrong gas – pure argon, valve open
Back cap not seated (O-ring inside the body)
Wrong tungsten type
Gas off too soon – keep flowing ~1 s per 10 A after the arc stops
Dipped into the pool – hold 2–5 mm off the work
Filler touched the tungsten – feed into the front of the pool
Wrong gas, poor flow or leaks
Dirty base metal or filler wire
Wrong filler wire
Torch on DC+
Arc too long – 2–5 mm
Tungsten contaminated or ground across – snap off ~10 mm, regrind lengthways
Poor gas flow
Dirty metal or filler
Check setup, gas on and flowing
Wrong tungsten size/type
Loose connections; earth clamp straight onto the job
Earth lead and cables connected?
MMA selected, machine on?
Arc too long
Dirty or wet job
Damp electrodes – keep rods dry
Amps too high (or go up a rod size)
Arc too long

stick.problem: Weld sitting on top / poor penetration
fixes: Not enough amps (or go up a rod size)
Dirty job, technique or joint prep
Too many amps or rod too big
Travel faster
Too much heat – lower amps / smaller rod
Joint design and fit-up, tack and stitch
Wrong polarity for the rod – check the box

flags: Manual quotes different gas flow ranges in different charts (6–12 and 10–15 L/min). Door chart says 8–12 L/min.
